nodes.summary: The Scottish Book Problem 88 claim is false: there is a real sequence $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ such that for every real sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with $|x_n| \le 1$ for all $n$, each series $\sum_n a_{m+n} x_n$ with $m \ge 0$ converges, as the limit of its partial sums, to some $L_m$, and $\sum_m |L_m| < \infty$, but $\sum_n n |a_n|$ diverges.
nodes.title: Mazur's Scottish Book Problem 88 fails

nodes.summary: The claim that every real sequence $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with the following property satisfies $\sum_n n |a_n| < \infty$: for every real sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with $|x_n| \le 1$ for all $n$, each series $\sum_n a_{m+n} x_n$ with $m \ge 0$ converges, as the limit of its partial sums, to some $L_m$, and $\sum_m |L_m| < \infty$.
nodes.title: Scottish Book Problem 88 (Mazur)
